opportunities.direction: Move the Watch app to a durable local write-ahead log: every set is committed to on-watch storage with a client-generated UUID and monotonic sequence number before any UI confirmation, then replayed to the phone via WCSession transferUserInfo (guaranteed, queued) rather than live messaging, with idempotent upsert on the phone keyed by UUID to kill duplicates. Keep the current Watch logging UI unchanged; add a visible per-workout sync state (pending / synced / N sets queued) and a manual 'force resend' in workout detail so users can see nothing was lost. Add a background refresh path plus a reconciliation pass on app foreground that diffs Watch and phone set counts and pulls anything missing.
validate: What share of the 442 reports are true data loss versus delayed arrival that eventually reconciles? Instrument sync latency and final delivery rate per session before choosing between transport and storage fixes.
Do failures correlate with a specific watchOS/iOS pairing (several reviews cite iOS 18 beta crashes alongside sync loss), or with phone-app termination mid-workout?
What is the actual WCSession queue depth and payload limit under a 60-set session with the phone out of Bluetooth range for 45+ minutes, and does transferUserInfo survive a Watch app force-quit?

opportunities.direction: Move the rest interval off an in-process timer and onto a wall-clock end timestamp plus a pre-scheduled local notification (and a Watch-side haptic scheduled independently), so elapsed time is recomputed from the timestamp on every foreground, complication, or Watch wake rather than counted down in memory. Keep an active audio/workout session for the Watch so the haptic fires even when the phone is locked or another app owns the foreground, and dedupe the phone and Watch alerts so only one fires. The user sees the same timer UI, but it shows correct remaining time after any lock or app switch and always buzzes at zero.
validate: What share of the 437 are Watch-only failures (haptic never fires) versus phone timers that drift or reset — the fix is different for each.
Measure how many of these reviewers also mention Watch sync failures (related theme, 442 mentions) to see whether one connectivity/session bug underlies both.

Confirm iOS constraints: whether a scheduled local notification plus HKWorkoutSession gives reliable sub-second alerting with music playing in the foreground, and behaviour when users have notifications or Focus restricted.

brief.markdown:
## Executive summary

This run covers 3,214 fitness-tracker reviews across 161 extraction batches, consolidated into 12 themes plus an uncategorized bucket. Two reliability failures dominate and both sit behind the paywall: Apple Watch set sync loss (442 mentions, 13.8%, avg. severity 3.7, rising) and a rest timer that dies in the background (437 mentions, 13.6%, avg. severity 3.6, rising), with reviewers naming the annual price in the same sentence as the defect [item:fit-0656] [item:fit-1923]. A third, smaller theme is the most urgent in time terms: launch crashes on the iOS 18 beta, 141 mentions at avg. severity 4.6, spiking from 29 to 106 mentions in the last two buckets [item:fit-0159]. The recommended first move is to ship the iOS 18 launch-crash hotfix immediately, then fund Watch sync durability and the wall-clock rest timer as the two features that must be working before the annual-pricing push. The price objection itself (259 mentions, 8.1%, avg. severity 2.5) reads as a value complaint about broken paid features and a too-generous free tier, not a demand for a lower number [item:fit-0190]. Biggest caveat: this corpus mixes IronLog with competitors SetCount and LiftLab, so theme counts are category-level signal, not IronLog-only rates, and sentiment accuracy against the golden set is only 0.68.

## Top opportunities

### 1. Make Watch-to-phone set sync lossless — score 90

442 reviews (13.8%) describe sets logged on the Watch arriving late, arriving duplicated, or never arriving, with whole sessions lost; average severity is 3.7/5 with 83% negative sentiment. The trend rises steadily from 18 mentions in the oldest bucket to 81 in the newest, and 42% of the theme is paid subscribers [item:fit-1913].

Commit every set to an on-watch write-ahead log with a client-generated UUID before UI confirmation, replay via queued `transferUserInfo` with idempotent upsert on the phone, and expose per-workout sync state plus a manual force-resend. Confidence high, effort L, impact XL.

> "Watch app won't stay connected, dropped my entire chest workout today, synced only 3 sets out of 12" [item:fit-1913]

> "Paid $79 for the year and the Watch app is useless. Sets sync late or not at all" [item:fit-0656]

### 2. Make the rest timer survive background and lock — score 87

437 reviews (13.6%) report the rest countdown pausing, resetting, or firing minutes late when the phone locks or another app takes the foreground, and no haptic on Watch; average severity 3.6/5, 81% negative, rising in each of the last four months (38 → 89). 52% of these reviewers are paid subscribers and many ask for a refund [item:fit-1923].

Replace the in-process countdown with a wall-clock end timestamp plus pre-scheduled local and Watch-side notifications, recomputed on every foreground or wrist wake, deduped so only one alert fires. Confidence high, effort M, impact XL.

> "Paid $79/year for IronLog and the rest timer is completely broken in the background. The second my phone locks or I switch apps the timer resets or stops notifying me" [item:fit-1923]

> "the rest timer is useless. It stops the second the phone locks or I open Apple Music. I'm sitting there resting and never get a notification." [item:fit-2525]

### 3. Fix launch crashes on iOS 18 before renewal push — score 72

141 reviews (4.4%) report launch crashes or startup hangs at average severity 4.6/5 with 95% negative sentiment; 73% come from iOS beta users and 41% from paid subscribers. The spike is recent: 0–2 mentions per bucket historically, then 29 and 106 in the last two [item:fit-0838].

Guard the boot sequence so store migration and Watch-connectivity init fail into a read-only launch screen, and add a crash-loop detector that skips last-session restore after two failures and offers local recovery of unsynced workouts. Confidence high, effort M, impact XL.

> "Absolutely unusable since the iOS 18 beta. Crashes on launch every single time" [item:fit-0159]

> "IronLog crashes on iOS 18 beta constantly. Crashes during workouts, crashes on launch, lost data multiple times." [item:fit-0838]

### 4. Ship CSV import from Strong, Hevy, JEFIT — score 68

306 reviews (9.5%) at average severity 3.1/5 and 70% negative say there is no way to bring history in; 84% of these items come from users switching from another tracker. Several state the missing import is the reason they will not pay [item:fit-1314].

Add a pre-paywall first-run import accepting Strong, Hevy and JEFIT CSV exports plus generic column mapping, with a review screen for unmatched exercise names and imported history read-only in v1. Confidence high, effort L, impact L.

> "No way to import from my old tracker. Years of workouts are stuck in another app and IronLog won't read them. Not paying $79 just to start from scratch" [item:fit-1314]

> "Switching from Strong was impossible. No CSV import, no way to bring 3 years of workouts over" [item:fit-2831]

### 5. Justify the $79 tier before the annual push — score 63

259 reviews (8.1%) raise the price objection at average severity 2.5/5, rising slowly, and 51% are paid subscribers — renewal risk, not only acquisition friction. The complaint is structural: paywalled features (Watch, charts, sync) are the ones failing, and the free tier is described as covering nearly the same ground [item:fit-0190].

Do not cut price. Fix timer, Watch sync and import, make import the headline subscribe reason, and redraw the free/paid line so paid owns multi-device sync, Watch logging and long-range charts. Confidence high, effort L, impact XL.

> "Paying 79 dollars a year and I can log workouts, but the free tier does exactly the same thing" [item:fit-0190]

> "Seventy-nine dollars a year and half of it is paywalled" [item:fit-0704]

### 6. Add grouped supersets and circuit rounds to logging — score 61

250 reviews (7.8%) at average severity 2.7/5 want paired, giant-set and circuit work logged as one round; sentiment skews neutral (59% neutral / 36% negative) because users frame it as a missing capability. The two most recent buckets (46, 41) are the highest in the series [item:fit-2637].

Add a group primitive: exercises bound into a round with one rest interval starting after the last movement, a round counter, and a stacked card on iPhone plus a scrollable round card on Watch. Ship with, not after, the timer fix. Confidence high, effort L, impact L.

> "when I do circuits or EMOM stuff on my Watch, I have to log every exercise separately and the rest timer goes off between each one instead of waiting for the round to finish" [item:fit-2637]

> "Makes the paid tier feel incomplete" [item:fit-1446]
